text: When you build a REST API, good design makes it easy for others to use. Start by giving your endpoints clear, simple names, like /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods, such as GET to read data and POST to create it. Always return proper status codes: 200 for success, 404 when something is missing, and 500 for server errors. Good documentation helps developers understand how your API works, so keep it clear and up to date. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications that depend on it.
